title: Legends of Horror at Casa Loma
note: nightly to Oct 31. The big one. Two kilometres of haunted castle, tunnels and gardens. Prime Halloween slots are already selling out.

title: ROM After Dark: Trick or Treat
note: Oct 30 and 31. 19+ costume party in the museum, 7:30 to 11:30. You are already there Thursday, so this is the night version.

title: Haunted ROM tour
note: weekends to Nov 1. Guided ghost stories inside the galleries. Add it to a regular visit for 5 dollars.

title: Fort York After Dark lantern tour
note: Oct 22 to 24, 29 to 30. Lantern-lit walk through the barracks at 7:30 pm. Cheap, atmospheric, close to downtown.

title: Colborne Lodge: The Unexplained
note: Oct 27 to 30. Evening paranormal tour of the 1837 house in High Park. Walk the park before it starts.

title: Queen's Park evening ghost tour
note: Oct 23 to 30. Free one-hour tour of the Legislative Building after dark. Pre-registration required and it fills fast.

title: Night of Dread parade, Dufferin Grove
note: Sat Oct 24, 5 pm. Giant puppets, drums, bonfire. Pay what you can. Grab dinner on Bloor after.

title: Halloween on Church Street
note: Oct 30 and 31. The street closes and the whole Village turns into a costume parade. Best people-watching in the city.

title: Black Lagoon pop-up bar at the Drake
note: to Oct 31. Horror-themed cocktail bar takeover. No cover, you just pay for drinks.

title: Halloween (1978) at the Revue
note: Sat Oct 31, 6:45 pm. Restored print in a 100-year-old cinema on Roncesvalles. Cheapest great Halloween night on this list.

title: Rocky Horror with live shadow cast
note: Oct 23 to 31. Roy Thomson Hall. Dress up, bring the props, yell at the screen.

title: Candlelight: Horror Classics
note: Fri Oct 30. String quartet plays horror soundtracks in a candlelit church. Very date-y.

title: Tales of the Damned, Campbell House
note: to Nov 1. Immersive horror theatre in a real 1822 house at Queen and University.

title: Dark Waters at Ripley's Aquarium
note: Fri Oct 30, 8 pm. After-hours 19+ party under the shark tunnel. Pricey but a one-off.

title: Haunted Disco, Broadview Hotel rooftop
note: Sat Oct 31. Costume party with a skyline view. Dinner in Riverside first.

title: Halloween Nights of Lights, Sherway
note: to Nov 1. Walk-through light show, the Halloween cousin of the Christmas one.

title: Pumpkins After Dark, Markham
note: to Nov 1. Thousands of carved pumpkins lit up along a trail. Needs a car or a long transit ride.

title: Shackled, horror escape room
note: to Nov 15. Dupont St. Escape rooms are a top couples pick anyway, this one is just spookier.

title: Screemers, Vaughan
note: to Oct 31. Seven haunted mazes plus midway rides. Classic scream park.

title: Halloween Haunt, Canada's Wonderland
note: to Nov 1. Coasters in the dark plus haunted houses. Last chance before the park closes for winter.

title: Bump in the Night, Toronto Zoo
note: Oct 27 and 28. Evening zoo with Halloween stuff. Nocturnal animals are the point.

title: Pumpkin parade, your local park
note: Sun Nov 1 at dusk. Carve pumpkins together on the 31st, then bring them to a park parade the next night. Sorauren and Withrow are the famous ones.

title: DIY: scary movie marathon night
note: any night. Pick three, rank them, order in. Counts as a date if you both dress up.

title: Distillery Winter Village opening night
note: Thu Nov 12, 6 pm. Tree lighting at 6. Opening night is ticketed, but after that it is free before 4 pm daily and all day Mon to Wed until Dec 13. Weekend evenings need a ticket.

title: Cavalcade of Lights, Nathan Phillips Square
note: Sat Nov 28, 5 to 10 pm. City tree lighting, stage show, and first skate of the season under the arches. Skate rentals around 15.

title: Santa Claus Parade
note: Sun Nov 22, 12:30 pm. Christie Pits to St. Lawrence Market. Bring a thermos. End at the market for lunch.

title: CPKC Holiday Train
note: Sun Nov 29, 8:30 pm. Lit-up freight train with a live concert off the side of a boxcar. Free, bring a food bank donation.

title: Toronto Fall Stationery Show, Parkdale Hall
note: Sat Nov 7. Small-maker market. Buy the scrapbook supplies for this project there.

title: ECOFAIR, Wychwood Barns
note: Sun Nov 8. Market plus the regular Saturday farmers market in the same building. Wychwood Barns is a good wander on its own.

title: Daniel Sloss at Massey Hall
note: Fri Nov 20. Dark, sharp stand-up in the best room in the city. Jim Jefferies is at Meridian Hall the same night.

title: Doja Cat, Scotiabank Arena
note: Nov 24 to 25. The big arena show of the month. Matt Rife is in the same room on Nov 22.

title: Canada vs Guatemala, BMO Field
note: Mon Nov 16. Men's national team friendly. BMO at night in November is cold and great.

title: Immersion dance festival, Betty Oliphant Theatre
note: Nov 8 to 22. Small-theatre dance. Pick one night off the program.

title: ROM, third Tuesday
note: Oct 20, Nov 17 · 4:30 to 8:30. Tickets drop two weeks before and go fast. No walk-ins.

title: AGO, first Wednesday
note: Nov 4, Dec 2 · 6 to 9. Two tickets per booking, book online. If either of you is 25 or under, the AGO annual pass is free all year.

title: Gardiner Museum, Wednesdays
note: after 4 pm. Ceramics, across from the ROM. Small enough for an hour before dinner on Bloor.

title: Aga Khan Museum, Wednesdays
note: 4 to 8 pm. Stunning building and gardens in Don Mills. Worth the trip up.

title: MOCA, Fridays
note: 5 to 9 pm. Contemporary art in the Tower Automotive building, then Sterling Road for dinner.

title: Bata Shoe Museum, Sundays
note: pay what you can. Weirder and better than it sounds. Pair with Bloor West brunch.

title: High Park loop and Grenadier Pond
note: now, for colours. Coffee from Bloor West, walk the full loop, end at the Grenadier café.

title: Evergreen Brick Works Saturday market + Don Valley trail
note: Saturdays. Market in the morning, then the lookout trail up to the Governor's Bridge view.

title: Scarborough Bluffs sunset
note: any clear evening. Bluffer's Park beach from below, Cathedral Bluffs from above. Pack a blanket.

title: Graffiti Alley to Kensington wander
note: any afternoon. Queen West murals, then vintage shops and a taco in the market.

title: Allan Gardens Conservatory
note: daily, free. Victorian glasshouse full of tropical plants. Great on a grey day.

title: Riverdale Farm and Cabbagetown houses
note: daily. A working farm in the middle of the city, then the prettiest Victorian streets in Toronto.

title: Leslie Spit (Tommy Thompson Park)
note: weekends. Five kilometres out into the lake, skyline behind you, no cars. Bikes make it easy.

title: St. Lawrence Market Saturday
note: Saturdays. Browse for free, split a peameal sandwich for 10. North market has the farmers.

title: Harbourfront sunset walk
note: any evening. Music Garden to the Spadina quay. Free events most weekends at Harbourfront Centre.

title: Bookstore crawl
note: any afternoon. BMV, Type, Ben McNally. Each buys the other one book they have to read by the next date.

title: Pick a neighbourhood you have never been to
note: any weekend. Roncesvalles, Leslieville, Little Portugal, Gerrard India Bazaar, Corso Italia. Walk it end to end and eat something there.

title: Toronto Islands ferry and walk
note: before it gets cold. Ferry is about 9 return. Ward's Island to Hanlan's, back for sunset on the skyline.

title: Rep cinema night
note: weekly. Revue, Fox, Paradise, Royal. Old movies, cheap seats, real popcorn. Check their calendars for themed nights.

title: Snakes and Lattes board game night
note: any evening. Cover plus drinks. College or Annex location. Loser buys dessert.

title: Private karaoke room, Koreatown
note: any evening. Around 30 to 40 an hour for the room, split two ways. Bloor and Christie.

title: Cheap eats crawl
note: any evening. Chinatown dumplings, Kensington taco, Little Italy gelato. Three stops, 25 total. Rank every stop for the restaurant list.

title: Jazz at The Rex
note: nightly. Small cover, two sets a night, Queen West. Sit near the back and talk.

title: Comedy Bar or Second City open stage
note: weekly. Comedy Bar on Bloor or Danforth, 10 to 20. Second City mainstage is more like 40.

title: Pub trivia night
note: weeknights. Team of two. Free to play, you pay for the pints.

title: Thrift outfit challenge
note: any afternoon. 20 each at Value Village or Black Market. Pick an outfit for the other person, wear it to dinner.

title: Arcade night at Tilt
note: any evening. Pinball and retro cabinets on Dundas West. Bring a 20 in loonies.

title: Skating at Nathan Phillips or the Bentway
note: late Nov onward. Free ice, rentals around 15. Bentway skate trail under the Gardiner opens in December.

title: Cat café
note: any afternoon. Tot the Cat Café in Leslieville. Small fee, cats included.

title: Cook a dish from a cuisine neither of you has made
note: any night. Shop for it at a specialty grocer (Kensington, Gerrard, Pacific Mall). Review it like a restaurant.

title: Escape room
note: any evening. Casa Loma has its own, Escape Games Canada in North York is the big one. Around 35 each.

title: Axe throwing at BATL
note: any evening. The original axe-throwing place, started here. Competitive couples only.

title: Pottery or paint night
note: weekly. Paint Cabin in Leslieville, or a one-off wheel class at Clay Space. Take the thing home for the scrapbook.

title: Marlies game
note: AHL season. Coca-Cola Coliseum. Real hockey for a quarter of a Leafs ticket. Toronto Rock lacrosse is the same idea.

title: Climbing gym day pass
note: any day. Basecamp or Joe Rockhead's. Pass plus rentals around 35. Bouldering needs no belay training.

title: Candlelight concert
note: most weekends. Quartet plays a film score or an artist's catalogue by candlelight. Pick her favourite one.

title: Spin ping pong bar or the Rec Room
note: any evening. Table time plus drinks. Loud, fun, easy.

title: Casa Loma, the normal daytime visit
note: any day. Tunnels, towers, gardens. Separate from Legends of Horror. Library pass may cover it.

title: CN Tower at sunset
note: clear day. Touristy, and you have probably never done it. Go up 30 minutes before sunset.

title: Ripley's Aquarium, regular hours
note: weekday evening. Go after 6 pm on a weekday to skip the kids. Around 50.

title: Food tour of one neighbourhood
note: weekends. Guided ones run 60 to 90. Or DIY: five places, one dish each, total 50 for two.

title: GO train day trip
note: weekends. Niagara Falls, Hamilton waterfalls, or Kitchener St. Jacobs market. GO weekend passes are cheap.

title: Leafs or Raptors game
note: season. Upper bowl starts around 80 to 100. Go once, log it, then go back to the Marlies.

title: Tasting menu night
note: book weeks ahead. Pick one a year. Keep the menu card for the scrapbook. This is where the restaurant ranking gets interesting.

title: Mirvish theatre or Massey Hall show
note: season. Mirvish does rush tickets some days. Massey Hall balcony is the best cheap seat in the city.

title: Couples spa afternoon
note: winter. Body Blitz or Hammam Spa. Thermal circuit is the cheaper entry, the packages climb fast.

title: Cooking class together
note: weekends. Pasta or dumplings at a proper class. Around 90 to 120 each, but it is dinner too.

title: Overnight out of town
note: a long weekend. Prince Edward County, Blue Mountain, Niagara-on-the-Lake. One per season.
